obligations.text: Apart from the facade's exception of spec 031 3.3 and rustev-node's edge to rustev-otel of spec 049 3.1, the only dependencies of a crate on an integration crate are the normal dependencies of rustev-jev, rustev-bedrock and rustev-serve on rustev-remote-http; make boundaries refuses every other edge, including these three as build or dev dependencies, any of them on another integration, and any other crate on rustev-remote-http.
No source file of rustev-jev, rustev-bedrock or rustev-serve is compiled from outside that crate's own directory; each uses spec 009's Part A machinery through its dependency on rustev-remote-http.

The change alters no behavior: every existing test, conformance case, golden, PlanId, recorded fixture and exchange record of the three crates and of rustev-remote-http is unchanged, and the public module paths of rustev-jev and rustev-bedrock still resolve.

sectionHeadings: 059: Shared remote transport by dependency, not by source link (amends 001, 010, 012, 030 and 049)
3.2 The source links become a dependency
record.summary: An amendment of approved specs 001 (3.4.4), 010 (I-2 and the `rustev-serve` note), 012, 030 and 049 (I-3). `rustev-jev`, `rustev-bedrock` and `rustev-serve` compile spec 009's Part A machinery from `integrations/rustev-remote-http/src/` through `#[path]`, because 001 3.4.4 forbids a crate depending on an integration crate. A crate whose sources sit outside its own directory cannot be packaged, so spec 031 3.4 keeps `rustev-jev` (and, for the same reason, `rustev-bedrock`) out of the release family until a reviewed change removes the source link, and leaves open how. This spec chooses the boundary amendment: those three crates may depend on `rustev-remote-http`, only as a normal dependency, and re-export or use its modules instead of compiling copies. No behavior, record, document or public path of any crate changes. Admission of any crate to the release family stays with a later change.
